links.outcome: Treatment disparity reduction and predictive accuracy after counterfactual fairness mitigation
links.effect: Fairness-aware counterfactual adjustment reduced treatment disparities by 64.8% without compromising predictive accuracy (AUC = 0.89).
links.quote: This approach reduced treatment disparities by 64.8% without compromising predictive accuracy (AUC = 0.89).

links.outcome: Bias in historical clinical data and NIHSS score interpretation across racial groups
links.effect: DIF analysis in 983,785 patients found minority patients required higher NIHSS scores than White patients to receive IVT, indicating potential bias in score interpretation.
links.quote: Using differential item functioning (DIF) analysis on a national inpatient cohort of 983,785 patients, we found that minority patients required higher NIHSS scores than White patients to receive IVT, indicating potential bias in score interpretation.

unlisted_practices: Differential item functioning analysis of clinical severity scores to detect biased interpretation across racial groups

screen.reason: Evaluated a counterfactual adjustment fairness-aware machine learning framework on retrospective inpatient data to mitigate racial disparities in stroke thrombolysis prediction.
